message: David, I've found Bruce Horner's work profoundly useful -- along with John Trimbur, he's one of the only people doing careful Marxian-influenced examinations of what goes on in composition. I think I'd have to say that it's impossible not to differentiate between the "economy" and the "ecology", though Marxians like Resnick and Wolff would say that the "logics" of the wired composition classroom are overdetermined by what you refer to as the "nomos" -- which in some ways seems to line up well with Bourdieu's perspectives on class. In that sense, "economies" involve many quantifiables not so much set in motion but (to use the terrible cliché) always already ( /cliché ) in motion, and then for the questions get kicked up to the next level of abstraction in Jarratt's etymological sense: how do we *talk* about the systems that value and exchange these quantifiables, and how do they connect in concrete ways to the material bodies and circumstances of the teachers and students in those classrooms?
